questions.text: Does the document explicitly explain the need for action on climate change?
questions.answer: The document clearly outlines the need for action on climate change. It acknowledges the unequivocal warming of the climate system, as evidenced by increases in global average air and ocean temperatures, widespread melting of snow and ice, and rising average sea level. The document also recognizes that this warming has occurred as a result of human activities and that adaptation will be necessary to address impacts resulting from the warming which is already unavoidable due to past emissions. The document further emphasizes that there is no alternative but to undertake adaptation planning, even in an environment of extensive mitigation. It provides recommendations for raising awareness of climate change risks, incorporating adaptation strategies into strategic management planning, including climate change risk management results into the Council’s risk management database, and monitoring and reviewing risk management context to identify new climate change risks and reanalyse all existing risks.

quote.content: There is no alternative but to undertake adaptation planning, even in an environment of extensive mitigation. The Fourth Assessment Report of the IPCC 2007a, indicates that warming of the climate system is unequivocal, as is now evident from observations of increases in global average air and ocean temperatures, widespread melting of snow and ice and rising average sea level. Global greenhouse emissions have grown since pre-industrial times, with an increase of 70 percent between 1970 and 2004, and a very high confidence that this warming has occurred as a result of human activities (IPCC 2007a). Adaptation will be necessary to address impacts resulting from the warming which is already unavoidable due to past emissions (IPCC 2007b).
